renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: purple_cn_profile
  title: Copy-number profile
  description: |-
    Each line is a fitted copy-number segment: its purity-adjusted copy number as a log2 ratio against two copies on the upper panel, and its fitted B-allele frequency on the lower one. It answers where the tumor genome gains, loses or keeps its copy number, and where one allele is lost.
    How to read: segments above the upper dotted line are gains and those below the lower one are losses. A BAF that rises towards 1 at an unchanged copy number is loss of heterozygosity, where one allele is gone and the other duplicated. Zoom on a chromosome to see the allele-specific copy numbers.
    Lines and annotations: the dotted lines at log2 0.322 and -0.415 are the copy numbers of 2.5 and 1.5, where the rounded copy number leaves two. They are a reference defined by the recipe, not a PURPLE cut-off. The dotted line at BAF 0.5 is the balanced state, since the BAF of a segment varies between 0.5 and 1.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/README.md
  kind: cnv_profile
  config:
    gain_threshold: 0.322
    loss_threshold: -0.415
  roles:
    sample: sample
    chrom: chrom
    start: start
    end: end
    log2: log2
    baf: baf
    copy_number: copy_number
    segment: segment
    label: label

- component: card
  id: segment_cn_spread
  title: Segment copy number
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median rounded copy number of the segments in view, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers the typical copy number of the tumor genome.
    How to read: a median of two with a tight box is a near diploid genome. A median above two with a wide box points to a genome with many gains. Filter to a chromosome to see where they sit.
  column: copy_number
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Copy-number segments
  description: |-
    Each row is a fitted segment with its position, rounded copy number, the copy numbers of the major and minor alleles and its BAF. It answers the exact fit behind each line of the profile.
    How to read: a minor allele copy number near zero marks loss of heterozygosity, and the label spells the total as the sum of the two alleles.
  columns:
  - sample
  - chrom
  - start
  - end
  - copy_number
  - major_copy_number
  - minor_copy_number
  - baf
  - label

- component: card
  id: driver_count
  title: Drivers by type
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of driver calls in the catalog, and the bars rank the driver types (mutation, deletion, amplification, disruption, germline) by how many they hold. The count beside it is the number of distinct genes. It answers how many driver events the tumor carries and of which kind.
    How to read: a deletion or amplification leading the ranking points to a genome driven by copy-number change, and a mutation leading it to point mutations. Open the oncoplot to see which genes recur.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/DriverCatalog.md
  column: gene
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: driver
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: drivers, by type
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: driver_likelihood_spread
  title: Driver likelihood
  description: |-
    The hero number is the lowest driver likelihood in view, and the box shows the quartiles of all of them. It answers how certain the catalog is that its calls are drivers and not passengers.
    How to read: high-level amplifications, homozygous deletions, homozygous disruptions and hotspot mutations score 1, while heterozygous deletions, LOH and non-homozygous disruptions are listed with a likelihood of 0. A lowest value of 0 is therefore often such a context event, and the point mutations in between are the uncertain calls to check before reporting them.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/DriverCatalog.md
  column: driver_likelihood
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: lowest, with the spread

- component: advanced_viz
  id: driver_oncoplot
  title: Driver oncoplot
  description: |-
    Each cell is a gene in a tumor, coloured by its driver type. It answers which genes carry drivers and which kinds of event hit them.
    How to read: a gene with several coloured cells is hit in several tumors, and a row with more than one type is hit in more than one way, for instance a deletion with a mutation. The side bars count the events per gene and per tumor.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/DriverCatalog.md
  kind: oncoplot
  config:
    top_genes: 25
  roles:
    sample_id: sample
    gene: gene
    mutation_type: driver

- component: figure
  id: driver_type_bar
  title: Drivers by type and gene role
  description: |-
    Each bar is a driver type, stacked by the role of the gene: oncogene (ONCO) or tumor suppressor (TSG). It answers whether the drivers act by activating oncogenes or by silencing tumor suppressors.
    How to read: deletions and loss-of-function mutations fall on tumor suppressors, and amplifications and hotspot mutations on oncogenes. A bar that breaks this pattern is worth a look in the table.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/DriverCatalog.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: driver
    color: category
    labels:
      driver: Driver type
      category: Gene role
      count: Number of drivers

- component: advanced_viz
  id: driver_record
  title: Driver record
  description: |-
    The card shows every field of one driver call. It answers the details behind a row you pick in the table or the oncoplot.
    How to read: pick a driver to read its type, likelihood, the method behind it and its copy-number range. A biallelic mutation has lost both copies of the gene.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/DriverCatalog.md
  kind: record_card
  config:
    labels:
      driver: Driver type
      category: Gene role
      driver_likelihood: Driver likelihood
      likelihood_method: Likelihood method
      biallelic: Biallelic
      min_copy_number: Minimum copy number
      max_copy_number: Maximum copy number
      chromosome_band: Chromosome band
  roles:
    id: driver_id
    title: gene

- component: interactive
  id: driver_type_filter
  title: Driver type
  description: |-
    Choose the driver types to keep. It answers which events the other tiles show.
    How to read: select deletions only to list the lost tumor suppressors, or mutations only to focus on point mutations.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: driver

- component: table
  id: driver_table
  title: Driver catalog
  description: |-
    Each row is a driver call with its gene, type, likelihood, whether it is reported and the copy-number range of the gene. It answers the exact content of the catalog.
    How to read: sort by likelihood to list the most certain drivers first. Select a row to open its record.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: driver_id

- component: card
  id: gene_event_count
  title: Genes with a copy-number event
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of gene calls that are not neutral, and the bars rank the calls (amplification, deletion, loss of heterozygosity and their partial forms) by how many genes they hold. The count beside it is the number of distinct genes. It answers how much of the gene set is altered and in which way.
    How to read: loss of heterozygosity is frequent in many tumors and is not a driver by itself, whereas homozygous deletions and amplifications are the strong events. Open the scatter to see how far each gene departs.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/README.md
  column: gene
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: cn_event
  top_n_count: 3
  filter_expr: pl.col('cn_event') != 'NEUTRAL'
  caption: events, by call

- component: advanced_viz
  id: gene_cn_scatter
  title: Minimum against maximum copy number
  description: |-
    Each point is a gene: the lowest and the highest copy number found over its exons, coloured by the call derived from them. It answers which genes are altered and whether the change covers the whole gene or only a part.
    How to read: genes on the diagonal have one copy number over their whole length. Genes above it change copy number inside the gene, so only part of it is deleted or amplified. Genes far from the main cloud with a deletion or amplification call are the candidates to follow up.
    Lines and annotations: the diagonal is the line where the minimum equals the maximum, so the gene has a single copy number.
    Note: PURPLE calls an amplification above three times the sample ploidy and a deletion below 0.5 copies, so the call depends on the fitted ploidy and not on a fixed copy number.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/README.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    reference_line: diagonal
    reference_label: Minimum equals maximum
    x_title: Minimum copy number over the gene
    y_title: Maximum copy number over the gene
    top_n_labels: 10
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    x: min_copy_number
    y: max_copy_number
    label: gene
    color: cn_event

- component: advanced_viz
  id: gene_cn_record
  title: Gene record
  description: |-
    The card shows every field of one gene. It answers the details behind a row you pick in the table or the scatter.
    How to read: a minimum minor allele copy number near zero is loss of heterozygosity, and the copy number relative to ploidy tells whether the gene is high or low for this tumor.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/README.md
  kind: record_card
  config:
    labels:
      min_copy_number: Minimum copy number
      max_copy_number: Maximum copy number
      min_minor_allele_copy_number: Minimum minor allele copy number
      relative_min_copy_number: Copy number relative to ploidy
      somatic_regions: Copy-number regions
      cn_event: Call
      chromosome_band: Chromosome band
      reported_status: Reported status
      driver_type: Driver type
  roles:
    id: gene

- component: interactive
  id: gene_cn_event_filter
  title: Copy-number call
  description: |-
    Choose the copy-number calls to keep. It answers which genes the other tiles show.
    How to read: select amplifications and deletions to leave out the neutral genes and the loss of heterozygosity.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: cn_event

- component: table
  id: gene_cn_table
  title: Gene copy numbers
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene with its location, its minimum and maximum copy number, its minimum minor allele copy number and its call. It answers the exact copy number behind each point of the scatter.
    How to read: sort by minimum copy number to list the deleted genes first. Select a row to open its record.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: gene

- component: advanced_viz
  id: protein_change_needles
  title: Protein changes along the gene
  description: |-
    Each needle is a somatic change at a residue of a gene, coloured by its coding effect and sized by the purity-adjusted allele frequency. It answers where along the protein the changes fall and how many cells carry them.
    How to read: needles that stack at one residue are a hotspot, and needles clustered in a region point to a functional domain. A tall needle is a change present in most tumor cells, which makes it an early event.
    Note: the allele frequency is adjusted for tumor purity by PURPLE, so it estimates the share of tumor cells and not of all cells.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/README.md
  kind: lollipop
  config:
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    feature_id: entity
    position: position
    category: category
    label: label
    effect: value

- component: advanced_viz
  id: protein_change_structure
  title: Changes on the 3D structure
  description: |-
    Each marked residue is a somatic change mapped onto the 3D structure of its protein, coloured by coding effect. It answers where in the folded protein the changes sit.
    How to read: changes that fall next to each other in space, even when far apart in the sequence, can act on the same site. Pick a residue on the lollipop to move to it here.
  kind: molecule_3d
  roles:
    position: position
    entity: entity
    gene: entity
    value: value
    category: category
    ref_aa: ref_aa
    alt_aa: alt_aa
    label: label

- component: card
  id: protein_change_count
  title: Protein changes by effect
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of protein changes in view, and the bars rank the coding effects by how many they hold. The count beside it is the number of distinct changes. It answers how many residues are altered and how.
    How to read: missense changes usually lead, and a high share of nonsense or frameshift changes points to loss of function. Synonymous changes do not alter the protein.
  column: label
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: category
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: changes, by coding effect

- component: interactive
  id: protein_gene_filter
  title: Gene
  description: |-
    Choose one gene. It answers which protein the lollipop and the structure show.
    How to read: pick a gene to see its changes along the sequence and on the structure.
  interactive_type: Select
  column_name: entity

- component: interactive
  id: protein_category_filter
  title: Coding effect
  description: |-
    Choose the coding effects to keep. It answers which kinds of change the other tiles show.
    How to read: keep missense changes alone to leave out the synonymous ones.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: category

- component: table
  id: protein_change_table
  title: Protein changes
  description: |-
    Each row is a somatic change with its gene, residue, amino acids, coding effect, allele frequency and the flags for biallelic, hotspot and reported. It answers the exact change behind each needle.
    How to read: sort by allele frequency to find the most clonal changes. Select a row to follow it on the other tiles.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: label

- component: card
  id: purity_gauge
  title: Tumor purity
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median tumor purity, the share of tumor cells in the sample, over the tumors in view. It answers whether the sample holds enough tumor for a reliable fit.
    How to read: a high purity gives clean copy-number and allele-frequency signals, and a low one blurs them. The lowest and highest values are listed beside it.
    Lines and annotations: the marker is a purity of 0.2, below which PURPLE raises its low-purity warning.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/README.md
  column: purity
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 0.2
  threshold_direction: min
  caption: median, against the 0.2 warning level
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: ploidy_spread
  title: Tumor ploidy
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median average ploidy of the tumors in view, adjusted for purity, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how many copies of the genome a typical tumor carries.
    How to read: a ploidy near two is a near diploid genome and a ploidy near three or more points to a genome that has doubled. Check it against the whole-genome duplication flag in the table.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/README.md
  column: ploidy
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  id: tmb_spread
  title: Tumor mutational burden
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median tumor mutational burden, in passing variants per megabase, over the tumors in view. It answers how heavily mutated the tumors are.
    How to read: a value above the marker is a high burden, which is associated with mismatch repair deficiency or exposure to a mutagen. The lowest and highest values are listed beside it.
    Lines and annotations: the marker is 10 passing variants per megabase, above which PURPLE labels the tumor mutational burden as high.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/README.md
  column: tmb_per_mb
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 10.0
  threshold_direction: max
  caption: median, against the high-burden level
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: msi_spread
  title: Microsatellite indels
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of microsatellite indels per megabase over the tumors in view, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how unstable the microsatellites are.
    How to read: a high rate points to microsatellite instability, the mark of mismatch repair deficiency. The call itself is made by PURPLE and sits in the MSI status column of the table, since the README states no rate to apply.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/README.md
  column: ms_indels_per_mb
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: advanced_viz
  id: purity_ploidy_scatter
  title: Purity against ploidy
  description: |-
    Each point is a tumor: its fitted ploidy on the horizontal axis and its purity on the vertical axis, coloured by the status of the fit. It answers whether the fits are plausible and which tumors need a second look.
    How to read: a tumor below the line has too little tumor for a reliable fit. A status other than the usual one means PURPLE used a fallback fit or raised a warning, so the copy numbers of that tumor are less certain.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is a purity of 0.2, below which PURPLE raises its low-purity warning.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/README.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_value: 0.2
    reference_label: Low-purity warning
    reference_highlight: below
    x_title: Ploidy
    y_title: Tumor purity
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    x: ploidy
    y: purity
    label: sample
    color: fit_status

- component: advanced_viz
  id: tumor_record
  title: Tumor record
  description: |-
    The card shows every field of one tumor fit. It answers the details behind a tumor you pick in the table or the scatter.
    How to read: read the QC status first, then purity and ploidy, then the mutational load. A fail status in QC means the fit should not be trusted.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/README.md
  kind: record_card
  config:
    labels:
      purity: Purity
      ploidy: Ploidy
      fit_status: Fit status
      qc_status: QC status
      tmb_per_mb: Tumor mutational burden
      ms_status: Microsatellite status
      whole_genome_duplication: Whole-genome duplication
      loh_fraction: Fraction with LOH
      contamination: Contamination
  roles:
    id: sample

- component: table
  id: fit_table
  title: Purity and QC table
  description: |-
    Each row is a tumor with its purity, ploidy, fit status, mutational load and QC checks. It answers the exact fit and the verdict behind every tile of the tab.
    How to read: start with the QC status, which PURPLE fails for contamination above 10% and warns about for a low purity or a noisy copy-number profile. Select a row to open its record.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/README.md
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: sample

- component: card
  id: variant_count
  title: Somatic variants
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of passing somatic calls, and the bars rank the variant types (SNV, MNV, indel) by how many they hold. The count beside it is the number of distinct sites. It answers how many variants the tumors carry and of which kind.
    How to read: SNVs usually lead. A high share of indels can point to a defect in mismatch repair. Open the genome view to see where the calls lie.
  column: variant_key
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: variant_type
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: calls, by variant type

- component: card
  id: coding_variant_count
  title: Coding variants
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of calls that fall in coding sequence, and the bars rank them by effect (missense, nonsense or frameshift, splice, synonymous). The count beside it is the number of distinct sites. It answers how many variants can change a protein.
    How to read: missense calls usually lead and loss-of-function calls are the rarest. A synonymous call does not change the protein.
  column: variant_key
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: coding_effect
  top_n_count: 3
  filter_expr: pl.col('coding_effect').is_in(['MISSENSE', 'NONSENSE_OR_FRAMESHIFT', 'SPLICE', 'SYNONYMOUS'])
  caption: calls, by coding effect

- component: card
  id: purity_adjusted_af_spread
  title: Purity-adjusted allele frequency
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median purity-adjusted allele frequency of the calls in view, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers what share of tumor cells carry a typical variant.
    How to read: clonal heterozygous variants sit near 0.5 on a diploid region and higher on a region of higher copy number. A low box means many variants are subclonal.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/README.md
  column: purple_af
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  id: variant_cn_spread
  title: Variant copy number
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median copy number of the variants in view, the number of copies of the genome that carry each one, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how many copies of a locus carry a typical variant.
    How to read: a clonal variant has a copy number near one, and values well below one point to a subclonal variant. Higher values are variants on amplified regions.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/README.md
  column: variant_copy_number
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: figure
  id: purity_adjusted_af_histogram
  title: Allele frequency distribution
  description: |-
    Each bar counts the variants in a range of purity-adjusted allele frequency, stacked by variant type. It answers how the variants divide between clonal and subclonal ones.
    How to read: a peak near 0.5 is the clonal heterozygous variants of a diploid tumor, and a second peak at lower frequency is a subclone. Peaks shift to the right on regions with more than two copies.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/README.md
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: purple_af
    color: variant_type
    labels:
      purple_af: Purity-adjusted allele frequency
      variant_type: Variant type
      count: Number of variants

- component: figure
  id: variant_cn_histogram
  title: Variant copy-number distribution
  description: |-
    Each bar counts the variants in a range of variant copy number, stacked by variant type. It answers how many copies of the genome carry each variant, and how many are subclonal.
    How to read: a main peak near one is the clonal variants, and variants below it are subclonal. PURPLE marks a fitted peak as subclonal when its variant copy number is below 0.85.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/README.md
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: variant_copy_number
    color: variant_type
    labels:
      variant_copy_number: Variant copy number
      variant_type: Variant type
      count: Number of variants

- component: advanced_viz
  id: somatic_variant_genome
  title: Variants along the genome
  description: |-
    Each point is a somatic variant placed on its chromosome, with its purity-adjusted allele frequency on the vertical axis, coloured by variant type. It answers where the variants lie and how clonal they are.
    How to read: clusters of points in one region are a hypermutated segment, and a band at a higher frequency over a region is a gain of the copy carrying the variants. Zoom into a region and pick a point to open its row in the table.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/purple/README.md
  kind: genome_view
  config:
    score_title: Purity-adjusted allele frequency
  roles:
    chr: chrom
    pos: pos
    score: purple_af
    feature: variant_key
    sample: sample
    category: variant_type

- component: interactive
  id: coding_effect_filter
  title: Coding effect
  description: |-
    Choose the coding effects to keep. It answers which variants the other tiles show.
    How to read: keep missense and loss-of-function effects to leave out the variants outside coding sequence.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: coding_effect

- component: table
  id: somatic_variant_table
  title: Somatic variants table
  description: |-
    Each row is a passing somatic call with its locus, alleles, gene, effect, allele frequency, copy numbers and flags. It answers the exact content behind each tile.
    How to read: sort by allele frequency to find the clonal variants, and filter on hotspot or reported to find the likely drivers. Select a row to follow it on the other tiles.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: variant_key
